title: Kernel auto-selection telemetry + debug dumps for perf suite attribution
creator: Mateo Alvarez
description:
Context
- We are seeing perf deltas (especially tail latency) that are hard to attribute because kernel auto-selection can change silently between builds, configs, and SKUs.
- For Q1 2026 baseline runs and ongoing perf-canary gating, we need to be able to answer: “Which kernel did we actually run, in which sequence-length regime, and did we fallback? Why?”

Goal
Expose kernel choice decisions per run (or sampled):
- Selected kernel identifier (stable, comparable across builds when possible)
- Sequence-length regime used for the decision (prefill/context + decode)
- Fallback information (was this a fallback? what reason?)

This data must be linkable to perf suite artifacts (run manifest + traces/dashboards) to make regressions attributable.

Non-goals
- Do not build a new kernel selection policy in this ticket (we are only adding observability).
- Do not emit per-token kernel events (too heavy). We only need selection decisions at request/batch boundaries.

Proposed outputs
1) Perf-run debug dump (always-on in perf suite)
- Artifact written alongside perf run outputs (same run_id as ADR-0172 manifest).
- Format: JSONL (one event per selection decision), gzip’d for large runs.
- Intended for offline diffing across builds and as a dashboard drill-down link.

2) Runtime telemetry (sampled in production, gated)
- Lightweight counters/histograms + a sampled structured log event.
- Sampling default off in prod; perf mode sets sampling=1.0 and emits full decision records.

Event schema (v1)
Required fields:
- run_id: string (present in perf mode; empty or omitted in prod)
- build_id / git_sha
- model_id + model_revision
- gpu_sku (e.g., H100-SXM, A100-80GB, L40S)
- region
- kernel_selector_version (bump when selection logic changes)
- selection_scope: request | batch
- seq_regime: prefill_tokens_bucket + decode_tokens_bucket (e.g., prefill=[0-512, 512-2k, 2k-8k, 8k+] and decode=[0-64, 64-256, 256-1k, 1k+])
- selected_kernel: stable name + internal id (e.g., “paged_attn_v3_triton” + “k_0x19af…”) and any relevant variant tags (bf16/fp16/int8, flash/paged, etc.)
- selector_path: auto | pinned | forced
- fallback: true/false
- fallback_reason (enum, if fallback=true)

Fallback reason enum (initial set)
- UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE
- UNSUPPORTED_DTYPE
- SEQ_TOO_LONG
- GPU_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH
- DRIVER_CUDA_CONSTRAINT
- KERNEL_INIT_FAILED
- BLACKLISTED
- OUT_OF_MEMORY_GUARD
- UNKNOWN

Overhead / safety constraints
- Perf suite mode: acceptable to emit verbose dumps; must not change kernel selection behavior.
- Prod mode: sampled (target <=0.1% of requests), and must be safe under overload (drop-on-backpressure).
- Ensure no prompt text or user content is logged.

Integration points
- Run manifest linkage (ADR-0172): include “kernel_selector_version” and “kernel_telemetry_enabled” in manifest metadata so diffs are explainable.
- Tracing: if correlation_id already exists (ENG-4826), include it in the event to tie to scheduler batch assembly + queue time.
- Dashboards: later ticket (ENG-4829) will link panels to the debug dump artifact for drill-down.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Perf suite run produces a kernel selection dump artifact (JSONL) with run_id and required fields.
- [x] Baseline dashboards can be manually explained for at least one known perf cliff by pointing to kernel selection changes (verify in a test run).
- [x] Fallback reasons are emitted deterministically (no free-form strings) to support aggregation.
- [x] Default prod behavior is no additional logging unless explicitly enabled.
- [x] Documentation: short README in runtime repo on how to enable + where artifacts live in perf suite runs.

Test plan
- Unit: selection decision event serialization; fallback reason mapping.
- Integration: run on H100 + A100 with contrived seq-length regimes to force at least 2 different kernels + a fallback path.
- Perf sanity: verify <1% overhead in perf mode for a representative run; verify negligible overhead in prod sampling mode.

Links
- ADR-0172 (metrics + run manifest): Confluence /architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0172-benchmark-metrics-and-run-manifest-format
- Kernel selection matrix (baseline expectations): Confluence /eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-selection-matrix-q1-2026
- Related PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood/pr-21519-add-kernel-selection-debug-dump-for-perf-runs.json
comments: 2025-12-05 (Yuki Sato): Drafted event schema + fallback reason enum. Syncing with Hiro on which kernel identifiers are stable across builds; current plan is stable_name + internal numeric id + selector_version.

2025-12-09 (Hiro Tanaka): Please include dtype/quantization tags on selected_kernel (bf16/fp16/int8) and a “variant” string for flash/paged. Also add an explicit selector_path so we can separate pinned baseline runs from true auto-selection.

2025-12-11 (Sofia Ivanova): If possible, include batch_size and prefill/decode token counts aggregated at batch boundary. Useful to correlate kernel choices with scheduler batching and p99 TTFT spikes.

2025-12-15 (Sean Gallagher): Prod sampling must be hard-off by default and drop-on-backpressure. We’ve been burned by “debug logs” under overload. Prefer emitting counters always (cheap), and only emit structured events when enabled.
2026-01-08 (Yuki Sato): Implemented JSONL dump behind perf flag. Added selector_version and seq buckets. Still missing correlation_id wiring; waiting on ENG-4826 landing in runtime main.

2026-01-14 (Mateo Alvarez): Please validate this solves the ‘mystery p99’ case we saw in long-prefill. Run one A/B run where only kernel selection changes (forced vs auto) and confirm dump makes it obvious.

2026-01-28 (Yuki Sato): Verified on long-prefill workload: auto-selection fell back to paged_attn_v2 due to BLACKLISTED (L40S) in >8k prefill bucket; forcing paged_attn_v3 removes regression signature. Dump clearly shows the fallback reason and seq regime. Marking ready for review.
2026-02-05 (Connor O'Brien): Approved for runtime-1.18 release branch. Confirmed defaults are safe: prod emits no events unless enabled; perf suite always emits dump artifact. Closing ticket.
